source_checks.note: The translated Interim Measures support the actual regulatory root: Article 4's core-socialist-values and prohibited-content duties and Article 14's requirements to stop generation/transmission, remove content, and take corrective model-training measures. The essay identifies its mapping from these duties to measured model mechanisms as inference.

CSET's current source page identifies the February 29, 2024 instrument as TC260 'Technical Documentation,' says it was designed to inform a future Chinese national standard, and says it provides the oversight department a reference. This directly contradicts the essay's repeated characterization of the document as a binding final standard or binding law.

The full translation supports the document's internal numerical provisions: over-5% corpus exclusion, suggested keyword-library floors of 10,000 total/200 per A.1/100 per A.2 category, refusal-rate thresholds of at least 95% and at most 5%, and positive-content testing during all conversations. Its use of 'shall' for particular clauses does not itself establish that the technical documentation is binding national law.

The Guardian's direct product test supports the disappearing-answer and leetspeak Tank Man examples and its Gemini comparison. The essay attributes these observations to the outlet rather than treating them as controlled research.
Promptfoo's published red-team method and results support the approximately 1,360-prompt test and roughly 85% sensitive-topic censorship result, within the evaluator's stated scope.

The peer-reviewed Pan and Xu study supports the historical cross-model evidence for refusal, avoidance, refutation, and fabrication. The essay correctly limits the tested model vintages rather than presenting them as a fresh 2026 snapshot.

R1dacted supports locally persistent R1 censorship, likely training/alignment origins, and experimental transfer of political alignment through distillation. It does not support the article's separate prevalence assertion that distilled variants ship worldwide 'mostly unlabeled.'
The USC audit supports the distinction between reasoning content and suppressed or rephrased final output on DeepSeek's hosted platform, with the article's 646-prompt scope preserved.
Steering the CensorShip supports the reported refusal-compliance and thought-suppression representation directions and causal steering experiments.
The independent Kimi K2.5 evaluation supports only the claims the essay assigns to that model and does not fill the disclosed absence of MiniMax testing.

The CEIAS report supports its four-model, 40-topic, 37-country design; 24% English versus 59% Mandarin insertion of state framing on the most sensitive topics; 42%-86% Taiwan failure range; and the reported OpenRouter spillover beyond China-only questions.
SpeechMap's published evaluation supports the Qwen-Max API-error observation and the distinction between open weights and hosted endpoint behavior.

Lin's local Qwen2 experiments support the cited sensitive-topic refusals, Mandarin/English asymmetry, retained nationalist framing after abliteration, and the author's attributed interpretation of policy alignment.

The analysis supports the cited 32.3% industry-wide contentious-request filtering/redirection/denial statistic and the reported time/model asymmetries, with those findings kept separate from Chinese legal requirements.
The Future of Free Speech study supports the comparison between rarer hard refusals, persistent soft moderation, and Qwen3's relative expressive-freedom result.
The government release is explicitly treated as an attributed government claim and does not carry the essay's legal-status or mechanism conclusions.

This secondary report carries the CrowdStrike code-security figures. The essay clearly labels them unreplicated, attributes them to CrowdStrike, and states that no conclusion rests on the missing first-party page.

hold_reasons: The essay turns TC260 technical documentation into a 'binding final,' 'binding law,' and a state punishment regime. CSET's source metadata instead says the document was designed to inform a future national standard and serves as an oversight reference; internal mandatory grammar does not establish binding legal status.

The claim that distilled R1 variants ship inside products worldwide 'mostly unlabeled' has no supporting deployment or labeling-prevalence source. R1dacted establishes transferability to studied distilled models, not global product prevalence.
unresolved_obligations: Correct the TC260 legal-status language throughout, clearly separating binding Interim Measures from nonbinding technical documentation unless an authoritative source establishes a different status.
Source, narrow, or remove the worldwide mostly-unlabeled deployment assertion.
